thread:
maria: Seeing a perf regression on hosted Qwen-14B with chat templates. Root cause looks like a kernel selection fallback when the prefix is ~1500 tokens.

maria: Profiling shows the runtime switching from our fused-attn kernel to the slow matmul path mid-request. Sample trace: 
```
hotspots:
  kernel_select  -> 12ms
  fused_attn_v2  -> 8ms
  fallback_matmul -> 98ms  <-- huge jump when kv cache grows
  kv_cache_update -> 15ms
```

maria: Happens reliably when the system prompt + few user turns push prefix length > 1200 and head_dim == 128. Not all models reproduce it, but Qwen and Mixtral variants do.

jamal: Is this only for chat templates (system prompt preserved across calls) or also single-turn?

maria: Only the multi-turn chat path so far. Single-turn-generation keeps us on the fast fused path even at 2k tokens. The difference appears when KV cache keeps getting appended (chat model does incremental KV inserts) and our kernel selector re-evaluates heuristics per-chunk.

priya: I suspect two interacting things: (1) our kernel selector prefers packed matmul for certain head_dim/seq combos, and (2) KV stride growth for cached prefixes triggers an alignment path that looks "non-contiguous" to the fused kernel, so it falls back. Also RMSNorm/SiLU model kernel variants have slightly different memory layout for the q/k projections which may exacerbate this on some models.

theo: Ran a quick A/B on canary nodes. Baseline (no change): avg latency 415ms, p95 980ms. Patch: "prefer_fused_on_chat_prefix=1" (env toggle) -> avg 330ms, p95 430ms. Commands: 
```
# run harness
python infra/bench.py --model qwen-14b-chat --prompt-file tests/long_systems.json --concurrency 8
```

maria: Nice. Can we make this a safe default? The risk is accidentally forcing fused kernel when it actually fails for other shapes.

priya: Proposal: add a two-step guard in kernel selector: if (is_chat_prefix && prefix_len > 1024 && head_dim in {64,128}) then try fused path, but fall back nondestructively with a cheap micro-benchmark per instance (5 tokens) to detect misalignment. If micro-benchmark fails, retry selector but record telemetry.

jamal: Micro-benchmark sounds good. Keep it opt-in via runtime flag and record a metric like `kv_selector_mismatch_rate`.

theo: I pushed a small prototype: `runtime/heuristics/chat_prefix_fuse` branch. Quick numbers posted above. Also added unit test that simulates incremental kv writes and asserts fused path used.

maria: Can we gate this behind canary deploy? I'll start a canary on eu-west.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for branch runtime/heuristics/chat_prefix_fuse -> 3 hosts (eu-west1). Watch `deploy/runtime/canary-chat-fuse`.

analytics-bot: Flamegraph uploaded: https://grafana.internal/redwood/flows/2417001234/flame. Short summary: "prefix-kv thrash causes kernel_select churn; fused path reduces mem copies by ~42%".

priya: Follow-up: also consider a complementary batching heuristic: if request is chat and prefix_len > 1024, prefer smaller batch sizes to reduce per-request kernel-switch noise. We saw a small throughput win at 4->2 batch.

jamal: I'll pick this up after lunch. I'll implement the env toggle, micro-benchmark, and the `kv_selector_mismatch_rate` metric. Tagging @priya for review.

maria: Thanks all — let's let canary run for 2 hours and gather metrics. If p95 stays <500ms and mismatch_rate <1% we promote.
